evidence.title: Single host-authenticated HTTP system-view route for Command Unified Work Queue
evidence.goal: Expose all six existing first-party Command Work Queue system views via one read-only HTTP GET path using a host-resolved current session and the existing owner ACL; no new view engine.
outputs: Go standard-library NewHTTPHandler accepting SessionResolver and existing Owner interfaces
GET /command/work-queue?view=... delivers six authorized existing view projections, GET absent view defaults All; no separate view routes
Host identity scope is never accepted from user query; no authenticated host → no data; host/provider access failure is all-or-nothing
Real HTTP tests for six view keys, no scope injection, missing identity, owner revocation, invalid method and route; CI and independent targeted L2
acceptance_tests: Existing six canonical Work Queue views are accessible through exactly one route using a trusted host-provided scope, with current owner ACL per item
No independent incident/tasks routes or revived team-load; query principal/tenant/environment and duplicated view rejected
Missing/revoked host identity and provider failure return no data or partial IDs
Exact SHA Linux, macOS, Windows Go unit tests and mandatory engineering kernel (including unchanged >=90% changed-security coverage) must succeed before any merger
No claim of production cookie/session, Shared Saved Views/Inspector, full queue workspace, persistence, assignment, paging or CAP acceptance

rules: Canonical: CAP-CMD-101 §§1–27 / Command Unified Work Queue, six exact keys from 06-command/modules/incidents-and-work-queue/saved-views.md; Command owns meaning and Incident/Task, Shared owns saved-view data and final Inspector.

Engineering: pre-existing epic E10-CMD-101, new bounded task E10-CMD-101B-HTTP depending on E10-CMD-101A-READONLY IMPLEMENTED (NOT accepted). Follows the repository complexity policy: one new runtime handler, one test file, no migration.
Code: product-runtime/work-queue/http.go, http_test.go, reuses unchanged queue.go Project and its exact owner authorization instead of recreating a queue engine. No framework or paid API.

Git: new child branch of integration PR #158; #158 itself is child of frozen security/SAST PR #157, whose exact HEAD engineering CI run 39352904407 SUCCESS. Neither PR #156 sibling nor any ancestor is merged or modified.
